The '''Myanmar census 2014'''<ref>{{cite news|title=၂၀၁၄-ခု သန်းခေါင်စာရင်း ကောက်ယူမည့် ပုံစံအကြောင်း တစေ့တစောင်း|url=http://www.m-mediagroup.com/news/9916|access-date=22 October 2013|newspaper=M Media|date=10 January 2013}}</ref> ({{langx|my|၂၀၁၄ ခုနှစ် လူဦးရေနှင့် အိမ်အကြောင်းအရာ သန်းခေါင်စာရင်း}})<ref>{{cite web|title=လူဦးရေနှင့်အိမ်အကြောင်းအရာ သန်းခေါင်စာရင်းဥပဒေပြဋ္ဌာန်း|url=http://m.president-office.gov.mm/briefing-room/news/2013/07/31/id-3930|access-date=22 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131023055933/http://m.president-office.gov.mm/briefing-room/news/2013/07/31/id-3930|archive-date=23 October 2013}}</ref> was a nationwide [[census]] between 30 March and 10 April 2014 in [[Myanmar]] (Burma).<ref name="first pic">{{cite news | title=Census to provide first picture of population in 3 decades | url=http://www.nationmultimedia.com/aec/Census-to-provide-first-picture-of-population-in-3-30214978.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131023060023/http://www.nationmultimedia.com/aec/Census-to-provide-first-picture-of-population-in-3-30214978.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=23 October 2013 | access-date=8 October 2013 | newspaper=The Nation|date=17 September 2013}}</ref> 100,000 school teachers counted the population at midnight 29 March.<ref name="IRIN">{{cite news | title=Challenges ahead of Myanmar's first census in 30 years | url=http://www.irinnews.org/report/97609/ | access-date=8 October 2013|newspaper=IRIN|date=8 March 2013}}</ref> The theme of the census campaign was ''A nationwide census – Let us all Participate''.<ref name="UNFPA">{{cite web| title=UNFPA staff to rally public support for 2014 Myanmar census| url=http://countryoffice.unfpa.org/myanmar/2013/09/27/8051/unfpa_staff_to_rally_public_support_for_2014_myanmar_census/| work=UNFPA Myanmar| access-date=8 October 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131023060344/http://countryoffice.unfpa.org/myanmar/2013/09/27/8051/unfpa_staff_to_rally_public_support_for_2014_myanmar_census/| archive-date=23 October 2013| df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref name="NLM">{{cite news | url= http://www.moi.gov.mm/npe/nlm/download/file/fid/713 | title=As census begins, Immigration and Population Ministry takes data of President's family | work=The New Light of Myanmar | date=31 March 2014 | access-date=3 April 2014 | page=1}}</ref>

== Introduction ==
{{main|Census in Myanmar}}

The government officially recognises 135 [[List of ethnic groups in Myanmar|ethnic groups]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/indepth/interactive/2017/03/myanmar-major-ethnic-groups-live-170309143208539.html|title=Myanmar: Major ethnic groups and where they live|website=www.aljazeera.com|access-date=2019-05-25}}</ref> Major groups include the majority [[Bamar]] ethnic group, and the [[Chin peoples|Chin]], [[Karen people|Karen]], [[Karenni people|Kayah]], [[Kachin people|Kachin]], [[Mon people|Mon]], [[Rakhine people|Rakhine]] and [[Shan people|Shan]], each of which gives its name to a [[Administrative divisions of Myanmar|state]].

The earliest recorded Burmese census was taken in 1359 in the [[Pinya Kingdom]]. The first nationwide census was taken in 1638, and it was followed by two other nationwide censuses in 1784 and 1803.<ref>{{cite book | last=Harvey | first=G. E.| title=History of Burma: From the Earliest Times to 10 March 1824 | publisher=Frank Cass & Co. Ltd | year=1925 | location = London | pages=194, 269–270}}</ref> The first modern census was taken in 1891 in the British colonial period. It was carried out in 10-year intervals until 1941.<ref>{{cite web|title=President U Thein Sein attends the meeting to clarify country-wide census-taking (2014) process |url=http://m.president-office.gov.mm/en/?q=briefing-room/news/2013/08/02/id-2497 |access-date=22 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131023061325/http://m.president-office.gov.mm/en/?q=briefing-room%2Fnews%2F2013%2F08%2F02%2Fid-2497 |archive-date=23 October 2013 }}</ref> After independence, the government conducted a census in 1953/54.<ref name="NLM"/> Two more censuses were taken in 1973 and 1983 by Gen. [[Ne Win]]'s [[Burma Socialist Programme Party|military government]]. According to the 1983 census, the population of the country was 35,442,972,<ref name="IRIN"/> and the Bamar accounted for 69 per cent of the population.<ref name="IRIN2">{{cite news|title=MYANMAR: Census offers hope to ethnic groups|url=http://www.irinnews.org/report/95462/|access-date=8 October 2013|newspaper=IRIN|date=16 May 2012}}</ref> The [[Burmese government]] estimated the population to be 60.98 million in October 2012, based on approximate reproduction rates.<ref name="spo">{{cite journal |last1=Spoorenberg |first1=Thomas |year=2013 |title=Demographic changes in Myanmar since 1983: An examination of official data |journal=Population and Development Review |volume=39 |issue=2 |pages=309–324 |doi=10.1111/j.1728-4457.2013.00593.x }}</ref><ref name="spoor">{{cite journal |last1=Spoorenberg |first1=Thomas |year=2015 |title=Myanmar's first census in more than 30 years: A radical revision of the official population count |journal=Population & Societies |volume=December 2015 |issue=527 |pages=1–4 |url=http://www.ined.fr/en/publications/population-and-societies/first-census-in-burma-for-over30-years/ }}</ref><ref name="spoore">{{cite periodical |last1=Spoorenberg |first1=Thomas |date=November 2015 |title=Myanmar's first census in more than 30 years: A radical revision of the official population count |periodical=Population & Societies |number=527 |pages=1–4 |url=http://www.ined.fr/fichier/s_rubrique/24592/population.societies.2015.527.census.birma.en.en.pdf }}</ref>

The census was taken in 80,985 areas across the nation. Officials prepared 41 questions for households and 11 questions for organizations.<ref name="NLM"/>

== Challenges ==
The census faces several challenges. In the past censuses of 1973 and 1983, the country's [[Internal conflict in Myanmar|ongoing armed conflicts]] put many parts of the country out of reach. As a result, several thousands of people (many of whom were [[hill-tribe]] peoples) in border regions were never counted. Another challenge is to ensure that everyone, regardless of citizenship, is counted. These include the [[Rohingya]] in northern [[Rakhine State]], who are officially classified as stateless,<ref name="IRIN2"/> as well as hundreds of thousands of immigrants from [[China]], who have illegally entered the country since the last census.<ref name=pks>{{Cite journal | url=http://www.ritsumei.ac.jp/acd/cg/ir/college/bulletin/e-vol1/1-3shee.pdf | title=The Political Economy of China–Myanmar Relations: Strategic and Economic Dimensions | author=Poon Kim Shee | year=2002 | journal=Ritsumeikan Annual Review of International Studies | access-date=15 October 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304052220/http://www.ritsumei.ac.jp/acd/cg/ir/college/bulletin/e-vol1/1-3shee.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref> Other challenges include a systemic lack of expertise—most of the civil servants who worked on the 1973 and 1983 censuses are now retired or deceased/unfindable, low levels of awareness among the population about the census, and the difficulty of reaching areas with active fighting such as [[Kachin State]], [[Shan State]] and [[Kayin State]].<ref name="IRIN"/>

The Burmese government plans{{When|date=May 2019}} in the 2014 census to count Burmese refugees living in [[Thailand]], who are estimated to number 130,000 people and Burmese nationals living abroad. Rohingya, described as ''Bengalis'' in Myanmar, will be counted under the "Other" ethnicity category on the census, along with ethnic [[Chinese Burmese|Chinese]] and [[Pakistanis in Burma|Pakistani]] residents.<ref>{{cite news|last=MYO ZAW LINN|title=Burma to count Thailand refugees in 2014 census|url=http://www.dvb.no/news/burma-to-count-thailand-refugees-in-2014-census/34045|access-date=31 October 2013|newspaper=DVB|date=31 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117032945/http://www.dvb.no/news/burma-to-count-thailand-refugees-in-2014-census/34045|archive-date=17 November 2015}}</ref> On 29 March 2014, the government banned the word ''Rohingya'' and asked Muslims to register themselves as ''Bengalis'' despite UN assurances.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.digitaljournal.com/news/world/myanmar-bans-rohingya-term-from-census/article/378773 |title=Myanmar bans 'Rohingya' term from census |publisher=Digitaljournal.com |date=14 February 2014 |access-date=30 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-international/no-registration-for-rohingya-in-myanmar-census/article5849870.ece |title=No registration for 'Rohingya' in Myanmar census |newspaper=The Hindu |date= 29 March 2014|access-date=30 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-26807239 |title=BBC News - Burma census bans people registering as Rohingya |publisher=Bbc.com |date= 30 March 2014|access-date=30 March 2014|work=BBC News }}</ref> In protest, most Rohingyas boycotted the census.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rohingya boat people: Myanmar's shame|url=https://www.economist.com/news/asia/21651877-poverty-politics-and-despair-are-forcing-thousands-rohingyas-flee-myanmar-authorities|access-date=25 May 2015|newspaper=[[The Economist]]|date=23 May 2015}}</ref>

On 16 March 2014, Rakhine mobs protested across Rakhine State, egged on by monk [[Ashin Wirathu]] demanding that the census be stopped or changed to prevent the Rohingyas from being able to define their ethnicity. Furthermore, according to ''[[The Economist]]'', "There are also fears of a backlash from Buddhist nationalists, should the census show, as many think it will, that the Muslim population is more than double the official estimate of 4 million."<ref name="cem">{{cite news | url=https://www.economist.com/news/asia/21599404-ill-considered-headcount-stirs-anger-and-mistrust-too-much-information | title=A census in Myanmar: Too much information: An ill-considered headcount stirs anger and mistrust | newspaper=The Economist | date=25 March 2014 | access-date=3 April 2014}}</ref>

== International support ==
The [[United Nations]] has agreed to assist the Burmese government in conducting the census. In the two years leading up to the census, [[UNFPA]] assisted in surveyor training and drafting the census forms.

The estimated total cost of the census is US$58.5 million, of which the Burmese government is paying US$15 million. The UNFPA is contributing US$5 million and Britain's Department for International Development (DFID) has donated over US$16 million.<ref>{{cite web |last=Watson |first=Angus |url=http://www.dvb.no/analysis/burmas-badly-needed-census-may-have-come-too-soon-burma-myanmar/38975 |title=Burma's badly needed census may have come too soon &#124; DVB Multimedia Group |publisher=Dvb.no |date=26 March 2014 |access-date=1 April 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140328133007/http://www.dvb.no/analysis/burmas-badly-needed-census-may-have-come-too-soon-burma-myanmar/38975 |archive-date=28 March 2014 }}</ref> The United Nations and foreign governments including the [[United States]], and [[Australia]] have pledged to help bridge the gap.<ref name="RFA">{{cite news|title=Myanmar Prepares for First Census in Three Decades|url=http://www.rfa.org/english/news/myanmar/census-09192013150846.html|access-date=8 October 2013|newspaper=Radio Free Asia|date=19 September 2013}}</ref>

== Population profile ==

=== Provisional results ===
Provisional results were released in August 2014. The data were from the Enumeration Area Summary sheets, completed by enumerators and verified by supervisors in the field. The provisional results provided the total population by sex and administrative unit, from national, state/region, district down to township level. It also showed the population sizes of [[Yangon]], [[Mandalay]], [[Naypyidaw]] and state/region capitals. Other information included were indicators such as sex ratio and population density.<ref name="popres">{{cite book | url=http://countryoffice.unfpa.org/myanmar/drive/SummmaryoftheProvisionalResults.pdf | title=Summary of the Provisional Results | publisher=Ministry of Immigration and Population | date=August 2014 | access-date=31 August 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903142929/http://countryoffice.unfpa.org/myanmar/drive/SummmaryoftheProvisionalResults.pdf | archive-date=3 September 2014 | df=dmy-all }}</ref>

The results showed that the total population is 51,419,420—a figure well below the last available official population estimate of 60.98 million in October 2012.<ref name="spo"/><ref name="spoore"/><ref name="spoo">{{cite journal |last1=Spoorenberg |first1=Thomas |year=2015 |title=Provisional results of the 2014 census of Myanmar: The surprise that wasn't |journal=Asian Population Studies |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=4–6 |doi=10.1080/17441730.2014.972084 |s2cid=154114929 }}</ref> This total population included 50,213,067 persons counted during the census and an estimated 1,206,353 persons in parts of northern [[Rakhine State]], [[Kachin State]] and [[Kayin State]] who were not counted. More females (51.8%) were counted than males (48.2%). People who were out of the country at the time of the census are not included in these figures.

==== Proportion of population ====
The most populated areas were [[Yangon Region]] (14.3%), [[Ayeyawady Region]] (12.0%) and [[Mandalay Region]] (12.0%). The least populated areas were [[Naypyidaw Union Territory]] (2.3%), [[Chin State]] (0.9%) and [[Kayah State]] (0.6%).

==== Sex ratio ====
Overall, there were 93 males for every 100 females in the country. Only in Kachin State were there more males than females; in Kayah and [[Shan State]] the numbers of males and females were almost equal. The rest of the states and regions had more females than males.

==== Population in towns and cities ====
There were 14,864,119 persons living in Wards (urban areas) throughout the country. This represented 29.6% of the total population. Yangon Region was the most urbanised (70.1%), followed by Kachin State (36.0%). Magway Region (15.1%) and Ayeyawady Region (14.1%) were the least urbanised.

==== Population density ====
The results showed a nationwide population density of {{convert|76|/km2}}. Yangon Region was the most densely populated Region, ({{convert|723|/km2}}), followed by Mandalay ({{convert|206|/km2}}). The least densely populated States were Kachin State ({{convert|19|/km2}}) and Chin State ({{convert|13|/km2}}).

==== Average household sizes ====
The provisional census results indicated that there were 10,889,348 households in Myanmar. On average, 4.4 people lived in each household in the country. The average household size was highest in Kachin State and Chin State at 5.1. The lowest household sizes were observed in Ayeyawady Region, [[Bago Region]], [[Magway Region]] and Naypyidaw Union Territory, each at 4.1.<ref name="popres"/>

=== Main results ===
The main results, released in May 2015, comprise two series of publications containing detailed national and regional information, and a report for each of the 15 states and regions in the country.<ref name="spoore"/> It contains text, tables, graphs and maps on the size and geographical distribution of the population by sex and age, marital status, education, economic characteristics, fertility, mortality, migration and the characteristics of housing units and household amenities.

The publication of main census results that require manual coding and further consultations is planned for early 2016. This publication will contain thematic analysis reports on the major topics covered in the census.<ref name="hmr">{{cite book | title=The 2014 Myanmar Population and Housing Census Highlights of the Main Results Census Report Volume 2 – A | publisher=Department of Population Ministry of Immigration and Population | year=2015}}</ref>

Migrants who had left to neighboring nations for work were naturally not included in population reports. A fair percentage had returned after the census due to undocumented labor crackdowns.
